headline: Eala Set for Asian Games as PHILTA Seeks WTA Exemption
seoTitle: Eala Set for Asian Games as PHILTA Seeks WTA Exemption | FMB News
seoDescription: Alex Eala remains committed to the 2026 Asian Games while PHILTA seeks a WTA exemption for her absence from the mandatory China Open.
deck: The Philippine Tennis Association is seeking an exemption from the WTA as world No. 18 Alex Eala chooses the Asian Games over the mandatory China Open.
author: FMB News Sports Desk

sections.heading: What happened
paragraphs: The Philippine Tennis Association has asked the Women's Tennis Association for an exemption for Alexandra Eala, who plans to represent the Philippines at the Aichi-Nagoya Asian Games instead of playing the mandatory WTA 1000 China Open.
Reuters reported Wednesday that Eala, ranked world No. 18, is committed to the Asian Games regardless of the WTA decision. Philippine reporting likewise says PHILTA is awaiting the tour's ruling.

sections.heading: What is confirmed
paragraphs: Eala is choosing the Asian Games during a calendar conflict with the China Open. PHILTA has formally sought relief from sanctions associated with missing the mandatory event. As of the verified reporting reviewed for this edition, no final WTA exemption decision for Eala had been announced.

sections.heading: Why this matters
paragraphs: The decision places one of the Philippines' strongest medal prospects in the Asian Games field while exposing a conflict between national-team representation and mandatory professional-tour obligations. Any WTA ruling could affect Eala beyond the Games through fines or ranking consequences.

sections.heading: What to watch next
paragraphs: The immediate development to watch is the WTA's decision on PHILTA's exemption request. FMB News will distinguish any confirmed sanction from currently reported possible penalties.

verificationNotes: Reuters independently reported PHILTA's exemption request and Eala's commitment to the Asian Games on September 16.
Philippine Daily Inquirer separately reported that Eala's camp was awaiting the WTA decision.
No final WTA exemption decision is stated because none was verified in the reviewed sources.
